name: Adult-onset Multiple Mitochondrial DNA Deletion Syndrome due to DGUOK Deficiency
aliases: DGUOK-related Adult-onset Mitochondrial DNA Deletion Syndrome
Adult-onset Mitochondrial Myopathy with Multiple mtDNA Deletions due to DGUOK Deficiency

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Adult-onset Multiple mtDNA Deletion Syndrome due to DGUOK Deficiency

criteria.description: Presence of progressive external ophthalmoplegia and/or mitochondrial myopathy symptoms
Identification of pathogenic biallelic variants in the DGUOK gene
Muscle biopsy showing multiple mitochondrial DNA deletions and ragged-red fibers
Elevated blood or CSF lactate levels supportive of mitochondrial dysfunction
Family history consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical manifestations plus molecular genetic confirmation of biallelic DGUOK variants and muscle biopsy evidence of multiple mtDNA deletions
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, histopathological, and genetic data due to phenotypic variability.

laboratory: Increased serum creatine kinase (mild to moderate elevation)
imaging: Muscle MRI showing selective muscle involvement
Brain MRI usually normal or nonspecific
genetic: Multiple mitochondrial DNA deletions detected in muscle tissue
other: Muscle biopsy with ragged-red fibers and cytochrome c oxidase (COX) deficient fibers

distinguishingFeatures: Often caused by POLG or TWNK mutations rather than DGUOK
May lack systemic mitochondrial myopathy features
Broader group with variable genetic causes
DGUOK deficiency specifically associated with multiple mtDNA deletions

redFlags: Rapidly progressive external ophthalmoplegia with muscle weakness
Evidence of multiple mitochondrial DNA deletions on muscle biopsy
Biallelic pathogenic variants in DGUOK gene
references: Spinazzola A, et al. Adult-onset mitochondrial DNA depletion syndrome due to DGUOK mutations. Neurology. 2009.
El-Hattab AW, et al. Mitochondrial DNA maintenance defects. GeneReviews. 2020.
Orphanet: Adult-onset multiple mitochondrial DNA deletion syndrome due to DGUOK deficiency (ORPHA:329314)
